dynasimR — Dynamic Agent-Node Simulation Analysis

A domain-neutral analysis and visualisation layer for discrete-event, agent-based and node-actor simulation outputs. The package is schema-harmonised: Profile A and Profile B share a loader and use analysis functions appropriate to their recorded outcomes.

Typical use cases include any system in which entities (actors, nodes, agents) move through states and interact within spatial or network environments — for example flow analyses, state-transition studies, resource allocation and policy comparisons.

The current version is an unreleased development candidate. CRAN and Zenodo publication have not been confirmed; use the source repository for installation.

Installation 

# Prerequisites for the complete quick start, including exports/dashboard:
install.packages(c("remotes", "xtable", "shiny", "shinydashboard",
                   "shinyWidgets", "plotly", "DT"))
remotes::install_github("cttir/dynasimR")

To install an unpublished local checkout instead, replace the last line with remotes::install_local("/path/to/dynasimR", dependencies = NA, upgrade = "never"). This installs required imports without upgrading existing dependencies.

SVG export uses R’s Cairo graphics device. With macOS R builds linked to X11 (including CRAN binaries), install XQuartz and restart R if its Cairo/X11 libraries are missing. capabilities("cairo") describes the build and does not guarantee that these runtime libraries can load. Failed exports report an error and preserve the previous output file.

Quick start 

library(dynasimR)

# 1. Load bundled example data (or point to your own simulation outputs)
sim <- load_example_data()
# sim <- read_simulation("~/my-simulation/data/raw/")

# 2. Time-to-event analysis
km <- km_estimate(sim, endpoint = "stage2", stratify_by = "scenario")
plot_km(km, title = "Time-to-stage-2")

# 3. Policy effect (policy A vs. policy B)
pol <- policy_effect(sim, policy_a_scenario = "A-S08",
                     policy_b_scenario = "A-S07")
cat(pol$narrative)   # ready to drop into a report

# 4. Autonomy-level trade-off
al <- al_efficiency(sim, al_scenarios = c("0" = "A-S00", "1" = "A-S01"))
plot_al_tradeoff(al)

# 5. Manuscript export
export_latex_table(
  data     = pol$effect_sizes,
  filename = "policy_table.tex",
  caption  = "Policy effect sizes.",
  label    = "policy"
)

# 6. Interactive Shiny dashboard
launch_app()

Analysis goal Key function

Autonomy-level trade-off (AL0-AL5) al_efficiency()

Profile B progress trajectory progress_trajectory()
Profile B wait-gap index compute_wait_gap_index()

Requirements

  • R >= 4.1.0 (base pipe |> used throughout)
  • Required imports: dplyr, tidyr, purrr, readr, tibble, ggplot2, survival, rlang, cli, glue
  • The dashboard requires shiny, shinydashboard, shinyWidgets, plotly, DT and xtable. dynasimR::check_app_dependencies() reports missing packages and prints an installation command; it does not install them.
  • LaTeX table compilation needs booktabs; tables with notes also need threeparttable. For an ordinary article template, add \providecommand{\botrule}{\bottomrule} to the preamble (publisher templates may already define it). Figure export supports PDF, PNG and SVG. Typical manuscript widths are 88 mm for one column and 174 mm for two columns; check the target journal specifications.

Data and interpretation

read_simulation() validates each scenario file before combining it. Keep summary/entity scenario IDs consistent with their filenames and supply both files for each scenario. A local scenario_metadata.csv is authoritative; your own data never inherit assumptions from the bundled example scenarios. See ?read_simulation and ?validate_dynasimR_data for the schema.

For Profile B, use progress_trajectory(), compute_wait_gap_index(), group_effect() and compute_completion_analysis(). The dashboard supports progress/completion overview, scenario comparison and summary-table export; other dashboard analyses require Profile A. Separate mixed-profile directories before launching the dashboard.

Policy differences and their intervals use A minus B, so a positive event rate difference is an increase in events. Bootstrap comparisons resample runs independently, not matched pairs. Entity-level survival/compliance intervals assume independent entities and do not account for clustering by simulation replication. Progress percentile bands describe the observed distribution; they are not confidence intervals for an estimated median.

Survival analyses need observed event or censoring times and binary event flags; invalid or missing inputs are rejected. Wait-gap calculations instead need observed activation waits: encode entities not activated as NA. They remain in the denominator and are not counted as timely activation.

Supply-demand ratios use supply / demand; zero-demand cells are undefined (NA) and counted separately. The deprecated eps argument no longer changes that ratio. The legacy morris_screening() function is a descriptive univariate standardized-slope screen, not a replacement for a designed Morris trajectory experiment.

plot_cost_effectiveness(..., show_ceac = TRUE) retains its legacy argument name but reports observed run fractions relative to fixed reference medians. It does not estimate reference uncertainty or a cost-effectiveness acceptance probability. Cost/outcome pairs must be complete; a zero effect difference has an undefined (NA) incremental cost-effectiveness ratio.

Manuscript placeholders are literal values, never R expressions. By default, fill_placeholders() preserves the source and existing output files. A template requesting an unknown or unavailable result fails before writing; use dry_run to inspect available substitutions. Exported table text is escaped as literal LaTeX content, so embedded LaTeX commands are not interpreted.

Development and validation

From a checkout, install package dependencies plus pkgload, roxygen2 at the version in DESCRIPTION, and rcmdcheck. TeX and Pandoc are needed for the full manual/vignette check. The following scripts work from any directory:

Rscript /path/to/dynasimR/dev/dep_check.R
Rscript /path/to/dynasimR/dev/smoke_test.R
Rscript /path/to/dynasimR/dev/doc_and_check.R

The smoke script exercises both profiles and renders real export files. The check script regenerates documentation without deleting unrelated files, builds a source archive, and fails on errors, warnings or notes. See MAINTENANCE.md for the audit, validation evidence and remaining release gates.

Citation

Cite the version or commit actually used and the repository URL, for example:

Heller, R. (2026). dynasimR: Analysis and visualisation of agent-based and discrete-event simulation output (Version 0.1.1, development candidate) [Computer software]. https://github.com/CTTIR/dynasimR

The earlier draft metadata named DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21889932. It is retained in the maintenance record for provenance; the public Zenodo and DataCite APIs returned no published record during this audit. Confirm publication before using that DOI in a manuscript.

Use of LLM tools

Where applicable, LLM tools were used for narrowly defined, non-authorial tasks: copyediting, prose refinement, Markdown/LaTeX formatting, boilerplate scaffolding (such as CI configurations and build scripts), and code refactoring. Tools included Chat AI, the KISSKI (GWDG) service, and self-hosted Mistral Small (24B, Apache-2.0) served through a local vLLM architecture on an Ubuntu Linux workstation with Intel processors and NVIDIA GPUs. Self-hosted use also includes models that were further trained (fine-tuned) or weight-edited in-house for specific tasks. All self-hosted models ran locally, with no data sent to third parties.

All scientific claims, methodological choices, analyses, interpretations and conclusions remain the authors’ own. Where applicable, LLM-generated material must be reviewed and revised before inclusion, and references must be verified against their DOI, arXiv ID or ISBN.

Local software setup: vLLM with Python/PyTorch, plus R and RStudio.
